shot.note: NEW 2026-08-25 per program feedback (4K rebuild) — added per the pattern in the sibling reel fellows/sai-pranavi-j/2026-08-17-why-ai-generated-code-still-needs-a-human/scenes.py's B00_TitleCard (v3 precedent). Title pulled verbatim from this sheet's own metadata.title ("The Pipeline That Was Lying to Me") + @HumanitariansAI, no VO. Silent-beat audio mechanics: compile.py's build_master_audio() requires ALL beats' audio_file paths to exist (all(p.exists()) check) or the WHOLE film's audio falls back to silence — a null/missing audio_file on this one silent beat would have silently killed narration on B01-B08 too. Generated a real silent mp3 (ffmpeg -f lavfi -i anullsrc=r=44100:cl=stereo) at mp3/beat-B00.mp3 instead of audio_file: null — 0.0dB silence, not narration, so the 'no VO' intent is preserved while satisfying the concat's file-exists contract.

beats.narration_text: I inherited a regulatory intelligence pipeline that had been quietly dropping real SEC filings — and nobody knew, because it never threw an error.
beats.new_visual_element: A calm dashboard feed — nothing looks wrong

shot.note: Calm feed log — SEC/FINRA/CFTC/FedReg rows ticking in, nothing looks wrong. Renumbered from B00 → B02 on 2026-08-25 (4K rebuild): two new beats (B00 title card, B01 executive summary) inserted at the front per program feedback; scene class, audio_file and manim src renamed to match, narration/visual content unchanged.

beats.narration_text: Five feeds — SEC, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission; FINRA, the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority; CFTC, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission; and two Federal Register feeds, one filtered for securities and investment filings, the other filtered to CFTC filings — funneled into a scoring and alerting system. Somewhere upstream, a filter checked that every item had a description before letting it through.

shot.note: Diagram: 5 RSS feeds -> normalize -> score -> Postgres -> email alert. Renumbered from B01 → B03 on 2026-08-25 (4K rebuild): two new beats (B00 title card, B01 executive summary) inserted at the front per program feedback; scene class, audio_file and manim src renamed to match, narration/visual content unchanged.

beats.narration_text: Using Claude Code to trace the pipeline node by node, we found a filter silently rejecting any item with an empty description — no log, no error, just gone. Turns out SEC and exchange filings routinely arrive title-only. The filter was treating 'no summary yet' as 'not real.'
beats.new_visual_element: Claude Code diff: the removed empty-description filter

shot.note: Code panel, diff view highlighting the removed empty-description filter. beats.narration_text: These weren't noise. These were real signal — exchange rule filings, an antitrust case — dropped before a human ever saw them.
beats.new_visual_element: Recovered filings: Cboe, MEMX, Nasdaq GEMX, DOJ antitrust

shot.note: [VERIFY: exact filing citations/URLs before publish — see FACTCHECK.md] List-reveal: Cboe Clear U.S., MEMX LLC, Nasdaq GEMX SRO notice, US v. Edwards LifeSciences. beats.narration_text: We dropped the filter, re-ran it against the live feeds, and verified the output against the production database. The result: seventy-three additional real items recovered — per run.

shot.note: Before/after count on screen: 297 -> 370 items passed. beats.narration_text: The sneakiest bugs aren't the ones that crash your pipeline. They're the ones that keep running — and quietly decide what you never get to see.
beats.new_visual_element: Silent filters don't fail loudly — they fail invisibly
